content: Your team should recognise Northbeam Sync at a glance. This LinkedIn campaign introduces a simpler way to keep files in step across devices, with a short headline and a clear product name. The attached banner uses a bright orange headline panel to draw attention to the message. The body copy stays focused on the day-to-day benefit and invites readers to explore how Northbeam Sync fits into their team's workflow. The design is intended for a public feed and should feel consistent with the rest of the brand.

The article image is designed as a simple title card, with the product name on a saturated deep rose panel and a short line beneath it. The body uses short sections and practical examples, while the image is intended to provide a strong visual break near the opening paragraph.

content: This slide introduces Northbeam Vault to a prospective organisation. The left side summarises the product's role in a team's file workflow, while the right side contains a short sequence showing how a file moves between devices. The slide uses a pale peach background to separate the section from the rest of the deck. The headline and labels are kept brief so the presenter can explain the details verbally, and the product name appears in the footer.

content: Your files should be easy to recognise and the message should be easy to read. This LinkedIn post introduces Northbeam Sync with a short headline placed directly on the campaign banner. The design team selected teal lettering on a cloud-white field to create a light, modern look. The post copy explains the everyday benefit of keeping files in step across devices and invites readers to learn more about the workflow. The image is included as the main visual in the post.

image.description: A square social graphic with a teal headline on a very light cloud-white background and a small Northbeam Sync label.

expected.why: The image has no alt text, and the teal text on cloud white also falls below the required 4.5:1 contrast ratio for normal text.
